solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: surface reading: a moment or place where a deadline has run out
setter's reading: the time is displayed up high, on a tall building with a dial

explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's up' is the phrase said when a period ends, but read literally it means the time is shown high above the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure carrying a big public dial places the hours aloft for the whole town to see.

indicators.note: 'after' places one piece behind another, telling you the order of the joined parts

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
rhyming slang: Barnet Fair = hair

explanation.surface: The London borough of Barnet swapping its representation for a Conservative seat at an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: 'barnet' (from Barnet Fair) means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture with legs and a back for one person is a common synonym of seat.

clue.text: Ring mobile phone: exploit hospitality for all

indicators.note: something mobile moves about, so these letters are free to shift position

blocks.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
taken as written, to be rearranged
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone told to ring a mobile number, then a note about taking advantage of free hospitality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' reads as one item, but 'mobile' is the signal to rearrange the letters of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding an informal gathering where any visitor is welcome means offering a welcome to everyone who calls.

clue.text: What’s taken up by chef in kitchen?

definitions.text: What’s taken up by chef in kitchen?

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue, taking something up means reading it from bottom to top, the wrong way round

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A question about which utensil a cook picks up when working at the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters EFINK sit within 'chef in kitchen' and read upwards give KNIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook constantly lifts a sharp blade for chopping and slicing, the classic tool of the trade.

clue.text: Remove top from dish for bird

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and removing it drops that letter

blocks.note: a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: An instruction to take the lid off a serving dish before eating the poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the first letter is at the top, so beheading BOWL leaves the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nocturnal hunter with large eyes is one example of a feathered creature.

clue.text: State flag raised on atoll originally

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards
'originally' points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter counts

blocks.note: to flag is to grow weary, to tire
RE means 'on the subject of', as in a memo heading
the opening letter of atoll

explanation.surface: A national flag being hoisted on a remote coral island when it was first claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner being hoisted, but it is the verb meaning to weaken; 'raised' then turns it upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the Red Sea coast of Africa is a sovereign nation, which is what state means here.

clue.text: Sailors round new piano for women’s celebrations

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the others

blocks.note: hearties is an old term for seamen, as in 'me hearties'
N is the abbreviation for new
p is the musical marking for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A crew of sailors gathered round a new piano, singing at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailors are not ABS or TARS but HEARTIES; N and P go between its second and third letters. A hen party is the British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a party held for a bride-to-be by her female friends before the wedding.

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone wiping out a tape of an operatic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two final words.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe a tape clean is to obliterate what was stored on it, so the verb phrase matches.

blocks.note: sick means unwell
William Shakespeare is one example of a Will; 'perhaps' marks the example

explanation.surface: A poorly playwright showing hostility towards others.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's first name is William, so he is one example of a Will.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or malice felt toward someone is the standard sense of the two-word phrase.

indicators.note: something prepared has been made up or worked into shape, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pharmacist selling iodine made up as a protective treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iodine' and 'preservative' suggest a chemist's shop, but the first two words are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax-seed extract is rubbed into wood such as cricket bats to protect and seal it.

clue.text: Church men in role writing material

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: an actor's role is a part
CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clergymen cast in a part are given scripts to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church men' reads as clergy, but it splits into an abbreviation and a plain word, which go together inside the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated animal skin was used for centuries as a surface for manuscripts and documents.

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An electrical conductor that carries a changed current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'current' suggest electricity, and 'contains' looks like a container signal; it is the fodder, with I added before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian maestro who led orchestras such as the NBC Symphony.

blocks.note: first meaning: to be in charge of, as a business
second meaning: to race on foot; the question mark flags the example

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea, managing to take part in a long race, but the clue splits at 'to' into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both operating an organisation and moving fast on foot in a long-distance race.

blocks.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a book that is out has been published

explanation.surface: A newspaper running a racy, scandalous story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something spicy' suggests gossip, but it is a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This highly seasoned French stew of meat and vegetables is a well-flavoured, peppery dish.

indicators.note: to consume something is to take it inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A household eating a cucumber she has provided.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the family the eater, and it is: 'good family' supplies the outer letters, which swallow the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small variety of the vine fruit is picked young and pickled, so it is a kind of cucumber.

clue.text: Flee easternmost part of remote southern headland

indicators.note: in an across entry east is the right-hand end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of remote
S is the abbreviation for southern
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Running away to the far tip of an isolated promontory in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: On a map east is on the right, so the easternmost letter of a word is its last.
explanation.definitionFit: To get away or run off from danger or captivity is a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Water frozen in kitchen oddly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Water left to freeze in the kitchen and then forgotten about.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of 'kitchen' and the even ones remain.
explanation.definitionFit: When liquid H2O solidifies below zero degrees it becomes the cold solid substance.

blocks.note: a gate is a way in
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, as gates at an airport are lettered

explanation.surface: A passenger moved through the airport by way of a numbered gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' looks like being carried somewhere through an airport gate, but it means enraptured; the number 4 becomes the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away with delight, utterly spellbound, is a figurative sense of transported.

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom to the top, the wrong way round

blocks.note: letters from inside the hyphenated term

explanation.surface: A band speeding up the beat in a pop-metal song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Speed' alone is the definition and 'up' tells you to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the rate at which a piece is played, its pace, is described by this Italian term.

indicators.note: something that involves another takes it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A discussion about the monarch's scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'king's' is read as 'is', a link word, so only R goes inside CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A map or diagram setting out a course or scheme can serve as a plan, especially as a verb: to map out.

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is dropped
'about' suggests turning around and moving things about, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written, before the deletion

explanation.surface: A Republican politician steering clear of a fight over faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About religion' looks like the topic of the skirmish, but 'about' is the rearrangement signal for what is left once R goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The monotheistic faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab is one of the world's major faiths.

clue.text: Gershwin say in restaurant asking for starters

indicators.note: starters come first, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A diner in a restaurant ordering appetisers, with the composer in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' suggests a restaurant menu, but it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin, the lyricist brother of George, is one person with this first name, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Irish with a question: one for Arab

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
taken as written
Q is the abbreviation for question
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Irish person with a query about which one is the Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: Four small pieces, all standard abbreviations, simply join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Iraq is generally an Arab, so the nationality is an example of the broader ethnic group.

indicators.note: something put off is disturbed or thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A stalled economy deterring a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like a verb meaning deterred, but it signals the rearrangement of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversary or rival who actively works against someone is a near-synonym of opponent.
